headline: Space Force spends big. Startups strategize. Investors eye IPOs.
deck: This week saw significant defense contracts and funding rounds, revealing the tight-knit web of aerospace and defense.

stories.head: SpaceX cashes in with $4.16 billion contract
stories.body: The Space Force awarded SpaceX a hefty $4.16 billion to develop a satellite network for tracking airborne threats. This contract underscores the importance of established relationships in defense procurement, where familiarity often trumps competitive bids. SpaceX continues to solidify its role as a go-to contractor for the military.
stories.soWhat: In a world where new entrants struggle, SpaceX’s dominance in defense contracts is a reminder that sometimes it pays to be the well-connected insider.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense focus
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, valuing the co-orbital security firm at $1.6 billion. With the Department of Defense increasingly pulling through for such startups, this funding signals a growing appetite for innovative solutions in space domain awareness. Investors are clearly betting on the military's need for enhanced security measures.
stories.soWhat: True Anomaly's success reflects a broader trend: as defense budgets swell, startups offering niche solutions are becoming the new darlings of venture capital.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has passed its critical design review, paving the way for further development. This spacecraft is designed to support various military missions, but the real test will be its ability to meet stringent timelines and budget constraints. The stakes are high as expectations mount.
stories.soWhat: Clearing a design review is just the first hurdle; the real challenge lies in execution, where many promising projects stumble.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's next moves
watchlist.body: With a $4.16 billion contract under its belt, SpaceX's strategic decisions will be crucial for its future defense projects.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's growth trajectory
watchlist.body: Investors will be watching how True Anomaly leverages its recent funding to expand its market presence in co-orbital security.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next steps post-review
watchlist.body: The real test now for Sierra Space is how quickly it can progress from design to actual deployment, especially under tight defense timelines.

watchlist.title: Potential IPOs in defense-tech
watchlist.body: With the defense-tech IPO window cracking open, startups might soon need to decide between staying private or taking the plunge into public markets.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
